hypothesis: PR #1164 (merged, docs/design/lever-decode-reproducibility-exposure12-seed47-measured-results.md) confirmed decode non-determinism across re-evals of an identical checkpoint+flags and recommended as its next lever: 'find/seed decode RNG (evaluate_model seed if available)'. This run tests the most direct version of that hypothesis: pin PYTHONHASHSEED (Python's per-process string-hash randomization affects set/dict iteration order, which is a common uncontrolled source of run-to-run divergence in tie-breaking code that was not caught by the CLI's own --seed) across repeated evals of the same checkpoint+flags and see whether that alone restores determinism.

checkpoint.recipe: twotower, context-backend=scratch, steps=16, batch-size=2, lr=1e-3, structural-bias=1.5, seed=47, device=cpu, asap-decode
checkpoint.note: Training itself reproduces bit-for-bit (last_loss=7.189 matches the historical exposure12 seed47 champion); the divergence is eval/decode-only.

decision_reason: Pinning PYTHONHASHSEED=0 across all 3 re-evals of the identical checkpoint+flags did NOT restore determinism: meaningful_program_rate still varies 0.333<->0.667, reward_score varies 0.765-0.860, decode_outcome_counts varies (model_valid count 0/1/1), and total_ms_sum varies 90012-132719ms (a ~47% spread) despite identical checkpoint_sha256, identical --seed, identical PYTHONHASHSEED, and identical CLI flags. This rules out both 'unseeded RNG' and 'hash-randomization-driven iteration order' as the root cause -- the seeded RNG in the grammar-fastpath lattice search (src/slm_training/dsl/grammar/fastpath/lattice_search.py:trajectory_orders) already derives from a fixed string key and was not the source of the divergence tested here.
revised_root_cause_hypothesis: The wide total_ms_sum spread (90-133s) on a suite whose per-record decode_timeout_seconds=30 nominally caps each record is consistent with the mechanism already flagged (not fixed) in decode-timeout-hang-seed44-steps72-finding.md: decode_timeout_seconds is enforced via signal.setitimer(ITIMER_REAL, ...) + SIGALRM, a soft real-wall-clock limit that CPython only delivers between bytecode instructions. If the actual generation call for a record is blocked inside a C extension (a torch op, the DFA/trie compiler search) that does not yield back to Python bytecode, the alarm is delayed until that call returns -- so whether a given record finishes as model_valid (full search, potentially minutes) or gets cut to fallback_output (~30s) depends on real CPU-scheduling timing at the moment of the call, not on any seeded/seedable state. This sandbox was independently confirmed to be running concurrent sessions during this window (three other autotrain PRs -- #1162, #1163, #1164 -- landed on main within the same ~10-minute span as this run), so CPU contention from sibling sessions is a plausible (not excluded) contributor to the specific magnitudes seen here, on top of the architectural soft-limit gap.
